_about: Parameters for the robot-workload-benchmarking rung-3 explorers. Every entry is copied verbatim from ../constants.json with its original 'class' and 'source'. NO number here is a measurement from any internal campaign. Classes: 'public' = cited public paper/doc, 'sibling' = a value already in a sibling kit, 'illustrative' = a round number invented to explain an idea, never a measurement. The explorers inline this same block in a <script type="application/json"> and also ship it here as a sibling file; nothing is retyped into prose.

wbc_control_rate_illustrative.source: illustrative control-loop rate used in A4; a learned locomotion policy at 50 Hz is a common choice

wbc_deadline_illustrative.source: illustrative: the period of a 50 Hz loop is 20 ms, used in A4/B3 as the deadline

perception_output_rate_illustrative.source: illustrative perception publish rate in A2/A0; soft-real-time perception commonly targets ~10 Hz

camera_frame_rate_illustrative.source: illustrative camera frame rate in A1/A2; 30 fps is a common depth-camera rate

window_illustrative.source: illustrative measurement-window length in C4; actual length comes from a sample-count rule

warmup_illustrative.source: illustrative warm-up before a measurement window in C4

foreign_cpu_gate_illustrative.source: illustrative census threshold in C4: a window is suspect if un-accounted processes use more than ~0.3 cores

interference_factor_definition.source: definition used in C6; the ratio itself is computed per run, no fixed value

cfs_default_period_illustrative.source: illustrative CFS accounting period in B0/A7; the Linux CFS-bandwidth default period is 100 ms (https://docs.kernel.org/scheduler/sched-bwc.html)

poisson_ci_level.source: Garwood exact Poisson interval, Garwood (1936), Biometrika 28; 95% two-sided is the convention in B3

p99_sample_rule_illustrative.source: illustrative sample-count rule in B3/C4: ~several thousand cycles for a stable p99; 3000 samples gives ~30 points in the top 1% tail
